Welcome to Highworth Combined School
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to Highworth Combined School and Nursery’s website. We hope that here you will find a flavour of the vibrant, inclusive and thriving school that is Highworth.
Prospective parent and carer meetings and tours conducted by the Head Teacher will take place throughout September, October and November. Please see our calendar (https://highworth.eschools.co.uk/web/calendar/189862) for dates. To book a place at one of these events, please contact Karen Bennett: 01494 525534 or reception@highworthcombined.co.uk. Please note that we like to limit attendance to 5 families so please be prepared to be flexible about when you attend.

Partnership with Parents
Parents and Carers
LIAISON WITH PARENTS
At Highworth we believe that education is a partnership between home and school and if each partner plays its part the child will benefit.
We place a strong emphasis on the role parents can play and encourage them to become involved in the school.
Most importantly we ask parents to encourage their children and support the work of the school.
There are many ways in which parents can play a fuller role in the life of the school and we urge those who are interested to take advantage of the opportunities available.
There are many ways of helping in school either on a regular basis - assisting in the classroom, listening to children read - or occasionally - on a school trip, sewing costumes for a school play etc.
All help of any kind is welcomed and appreciated, subject to completing a DBS check. Please ask at the office for the relevant forms.

Headteacher's Welcome
Our School
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Highworth Combined School and Nursery’s website. I hope that here you will find a flavour of the vibrant, inclusive and thriving school that is Highworth.
I became Head Teacher here in April 2017, but my association with the school goes back much further! I have been a parent, Chair of Highworth Friends, Learning Support Assistant, Student Teacher, Class Teacher and member of the Senior Leadership Team. Consequently, I have a deep understanding and appreciation of the values and ethos that make Highworth the very special place that it is.
The school community has worked together to define our ethos which is represented in the image of ‘The Highworth Carr’ shown below. These are the values that we hold dear, and which we will strive to develop in our pupils as they progress through our school.
It was pleasing to see this work reflected in our recent OFSTED report where the inspector wrote:
The school is passionate that all pupils will achieve highly.
They develop an understanding of the school’s values of ‘Curiosity, Achievement, Resilience and Relationships’. Pupils reflect these through being keen to learn, trying their best and working well with others.
A carefully considered, high-quality approach to pupils’ wider development prepares them thoroughly for life beyond Highworth.
They have positive attitudes towards difference and show empathy because they understand how life can be more challenging for some groups of people.
Across classes, behaviour is impeccable with pupils following instructions promptly and applying new learning swiftly. Around school, behaviour is courteous and considerate.
...attitudes reflect the strong ethos for positive behaviour across the school.
If, after looking at our website, you would like to visit the school in person, I would be delighted to show you around. I set aside time each week for prospective parents and to arrange a visit you need simply contact Mrs Bennett, our Pupil Administration Manager: reception@highworthcombined.co.uk, who will arrange an appointment.

Curriculum Vision
Curriculum
For 3 years, we researched and investigated how to deliver a curriculum that meets the needs of our pupils, taking account of our ethos, values and mission statement. We identified the following as being especially significant:
‘Memory is the residue of thought’ Dan Willingham
‘Learning is a change in long term memory. If nothing has changed in long term memory, then nothing has been learned’ Paul Kirschner
‘'You can always google it' is the most dangerous myth in education today’ Dylan Wiliam
‘Progress means knowing more and remembering more’ Ofsted
As our understanding of the research evidence available grew, it became clear that we needed a knowledge-rich curriculum, which was intelligently sequenced and fully resourced. It also became clear that there were significant barriers (expertise and teacher time) to us being able to develop such a curriculum ourselves. Consequently, we have hunted high and low to find materials that we could purchase from organisations better equipped than ourselves, but with similar ethos, values and intention. You will find a list of curriculum providers under the tab: 'Curriculum Overview; Whole School'
As a result, we have ensured that pupils in each phase receive a rigorous, coherent and intelligently sequenced curriculum, which builds on what has come before. Our curriculum is grounded in the strongest available evidence about how pupils learn and retain knowledge in the long term – focusing in particular on research from cognitive science.

Governors
Our School
Vice Chair of Governors
I am a mum to two boys at Highworth Combined, the youngest having joined in September 2019. I have always been fond of doing something for the education sector and started my journey as a parent governor at my eldest's nursery in Slough, in 2017, where I continue to be a parent governor as well. My day job involves working in the NHS healthcare sector, another area where my passion lies. I have experience in heading up health and safety as a parent governor. I think it is so important to be involved in a sector where your child is given so much, it's always good to give something back to the community.
I have lived in High Wycombe since 2011 and both by children attend Highworth. Professionally, I am a commercial lawyer currently working in the public sector. I feel, as every parent does, that my children deserve the best possible education. Highworth has seen a huge amount of improvement over the past few years. As a parent governor, I hope to be part of a team that can continue to move the school forward for the benefit of all the children.
Chair of Governors Co-opted Governor Business/Personal Interests: None I have two sons, Thomas and Daniel, who went to Highworth but are both now at secondary school. Thomas and Daniel loved their time at Highworth. I have always tried to be involved with their school, from helping in class or on trips and more recently with the PTA and being Class Representative, becoming a Governor seemed a natural progression. I enjoy working with the other Governors and staff at Highworth and making a positive contribution.
Business/Personal Interests: Member of Staff In my role as Head Teacher, I am very luck to work with a diverse governing body with a wide range of skills and attributes. I have had some experience of working as a Governor as my previous role involved me being a Staff Governor at King’s Wood School. I know that my vision for delivering the best possible primary education to your children is fully supported by the governors of the school and that we will be able to work in partnership, in challenging times, to achieve our goals.
Local Authority Governor
I have two young children both who are at Highworth. My youngest settled in so well and always has a smile on her face when we mention school. My eldest it just the same, he loves his teachers and friends and always looks forward to going. I am so happy that we found Highworth as a school for my children, as the teachers are caring, dedicated, knowledgeable and lots of fun! I am looking forward to working with the Governor Team to help develop the strategic vision of the school and support all the staff. I am currently a Secondary PE teacher at Wycombe Abbey. I am passionate about all this education and sport, and look forward to assisting the school wherever I can. Alongside this, I have experience as a governor at another primary school where I held the role of Safeguarding Governor and Link Governor for Assessment.
Business/Personal Interests: None I have been a governor at Highworth since 2007 originally as parent governor and more recently as a Co-opted governor. I have two children that have benefitted hugely from the education they received and from being part of the community at Highworth. My children are now at Unversity and Secondary school and have happy memories of their time at Highworth. I am currently Chair of our Premises, Personnel and Finance Committee. My governor duties fit around a busy family life and a career as an IT manager for GlaxoSmithKline. Although it is sometimes difficult to find time to fit everything in, being a governor at Highworth is one of the most personally rewarding things I do.
My eldest son started at Highworth in September 2020. When we first looked around the school, we loved the feel, the ethos, and the values it celebrates. We continue to feel that way. To me, this role is first and foremost as a parent, but I also hope to bring my skills as a management consultant working with the public sector to support the school to continue to go from strength to strength.
I am a newly Co-opted Governor to the school and am looking forward to being a part of the Governor Team. I am married and have two adult children both who benefited in the past from having attended Highworth school and the education and friendships they made there. In my professional life I am a Commercial/ Financial Manager working for Canon and have done for the past 30 years in a diverse number of roles. I believe I can bring some of the knowledge and skills I have learnt over those years to my role as a Governor.
I have lived in High Wycombe for over 25 years and my two children attended local primary and secondary schools. Professionally, I have taught in secondary schools and a middle school for nearly 30 years in various roles including 13 years as Head of English, also as an AHT and as a SENDCo. More recently, I have been developing literacy strategies within secondary schools to ensure all students are provided with the language skills required to become confident, independent learners. Throughout my career, I have been committed to supporting all students to reach their potential by identifying and supporting individual needs. I am looking forward to being part of such a thriving school community.
I currently have 2 boys at Highworth and I'm hoping to get my daughter a place next year. I've a corporate background of 15 years, most recently serving as a Head of Product for a Managed Service Provider. Outside of this, my passion lies with ensuring my children and their peers are able to get the most out of their schooling experience, with a focus on ensuring they're ready to take on the challenges of Secondary school, as well as starting to prepare them for life after schooling.
As a proud parent of two boys attending Highworth School, I have experienced first hand the exceptional impact this community has had on my children. Thanks to the supportive environment and dedicated staff, my eldest son has thrived in both his academic and personal growth. Watching him form meaningful friendships and grow into a confident young person is a testament to the school’s nurturing ethos. My youngest son, who recently joined Highworth, brings home a smile every day, excited by the learning and connections he is making. Professionally, I am a business coach driven by a passion for empowering others to reach their potential. With experience supporting individuals and organisations to achieve their goals. I believe strongly in giving back to the places that shape our lives, and becoming a parent governor is a meaningful way for me to support the school’s ongoing success.
I am a mother of 2 girls with my youngest in year 6 at Highworth. She joined the school last year when we moved to the area and has thrived in this environment. The ethos and dedication of the staff and leadership team is a testament to this. Being a newly elected Co-opted Governor gives me the opportunity to contribute to the school's ongoing success as well as giving back to the wider community in some way. Professionally, I am a Chartered Accountant and Property Manager in the private sector.
I joined the governing body in 2024 as a parent-elected governor and have a daughter at the school, as well as a son due to start next year. Professionally I am a security consultant, specialising in security risk and strategy development, leading a team within built environment engineering. I am passionate and supporting learning, and hope to bring my strategic consulting skills to help the school go from strength to strength.
